🔻 Ecuadorian fishermen sue US over attack on their vessel

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Sixteen Ecuadorian fishermen who were targeted in an attack by US Southern Command forces on their vessel in Pacific waters have filed a lawsuit against the US government, seeking compensation for the damage incurred, punishment of those responsible for the attack, and an investigation into the responsibility of Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa in the case.

In the lawsuit seen by The Guardian , to be filed in US district court for the western district of Pennsylvania on Monday, the 16 fishermen insist they had no connection with the drug trade and were illegally targeted by the crew of an unidentified US military vessel about 385 nautical miles from Manta, a port city in Ecuador, as they returned from a two-week fishing trip.
​
“The lawsuit states that the ‘manifestly unlawful’ attack on the fishermen came soon after Ecuadorian authorities inspected the boat for themselves and determined it was not carrying drugs, nor its crew affiliated with any cartels,” The Guardian said.
​
“It said the attack was illegal because, as with other strikes during Operation Southern Spear, it was conducted without congressional authority,” it added.
​
Additionally, the lawsuit alleges, “the wanton, willful and outrageous attacks upon, and kidnapping and torture of, plaintiffs at sea constitute torts under general admiralty and maritime law,” it stated.
​
“There is no actual armed conflict that could justify the use of military force against the boats, nor was there one on March 17 when the attack took place. The US’s campaign of bombings against defenseless vessels and individuals violates long-standing and well-accepted international law,” the media stressed.
